english.title: Carry out regulated procedure on animal which was shown live on television for general reception
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) carried out a regulated procedure specified in section 2 of the Animals (Scientific Procedures) Act 1986, namely **(..SPECIFY PROCEDURE..), which was shown live on television for general reception
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 16(1) and 22(3)(a) of the Animals (Scientific Procedures) Act 1986.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
carried out a regulated procedure
on an animal
which was shown live on television for general reception

investigatoraction.description: Guilty Plea by letter procedure may be offered for this offence

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Imprisonment for this offence will be abolished when Section 332 and Sch 37 Pt 9 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 are brought into force.
english.standardstatementoffacts: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) the defendant carried out a regulated procedure specified in section 2 of the Animals (Scientific Procedures) Act 1986, namely **(..SPECIFY PROCEDURE..), which was shown live on television for general reception.

other.penalty:
Three months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level four on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
Within three years after the commission of the offence and within six months after the date on which evidence sufficient in the opinion of the Director of Public Prosecutions to justify the proceedings comes to his knowledge.

maxfinetypemagct.description: fine not exceeding level four on the legislative standard scale
